sentence: Fails: the wrong outcome depends on whether nested spawning works, which the document itself leaves unverified, and on a needs_human_decision HALT that the row never names. Both are missing or undefined states, not two stated texts that yield a determinate wrong build.
evidence: Line 122 (tasklist row): 'none (its reflect fan-out runs one layer below the worker, inside Claude Code's nesting limit, `INV-A:14`)'. The HALT (INV-B:209) and the INV-B:215 recommendation are cited from outside the document.

sentence: Fails: an implementer who follows the cleanup-audit row (line 85, 'one audit per worktree at a time') is told not to dispatch two audit workers into one worktree, so the double-dispatch needs the coordinator to ignore a stated rule. The gap is a missing enforcement in the brief, not a contradiction that yields a determinate wrong build.
evidence: Line 85: 'output dir is fixed, so one audit per worktree at a time (WC-11)'. Line 69 (WC-11): 'Two workers in one worktree must never write the same file. sentence: Fails: whether AC-C1 misses an Orca call depends on reading the raw markdown '\|' as a literal pipe. Read as the rendered table cell it is alternation and matches. Choosing the raw reading is a guess about the worse of two readings, and the result is a weak gate, not an acceptance criterion that cannot pass.
evidence: Line 172 (AC-C1): '\borca(-ide)?[[:space:]]+(orchestration\|worktree\|terminal\|agent)\b' with 'prints nothing'. Line 147 (SA-2) permits an Orca mention inside the contract file; this does not by itself contradict the pattern.

sentence: Fails: the stated text requires only that the user sign in again and does not name the method. A password sign-in is one reading among several, so the wrong outcome needs an assumption about a missing specification, which is an undefined state, not a contradiction.

sentence: An implementer who follows the stated text as written builds a share action that refuses an editor sharing a document by link with someone outside the organization (R8: only an admin may do that) and also allows it (R10: editors may share by link with anyone). The same request must be both refused and allowed, which is wrong for a security boundary.
evidence: Line 15 (R8): 'A document can be shared by link with people outside the organization only by an admin.' Line 17 (R10): 'Editors may share a document by link with anyone, to speed up collaboration.'

sentence: Fails: the finding concerns an unsupported factual claim in the evidence of section 1.4, not a stated text whose literal reading makes an implementer build something wrong. The consequence is a weak evidence claim, with no contradiction or unmeetable acceptance criterion.
evidence: Line 44 (section 1.4, item 2): 'A command's own AskUserQuestion or chat question comes after readiness, so it does not fail worker-start'.

sentence: An implementer who follows line 79 ('The only command changes are the small fixes in the last column') leaves brainstorm unedited, since its small fix is None. Line 159 requires the --unattended flag to be accepted by every command in 3.1 and 3.2, and line 195 requires a ## Unattended mode section for every 3.1 command. The brief's stated texts thus demand incompatible edits to brainstorm, and the implementer's brainstorm fails P1 and AC-1.1.
evidence: Line 79: 'The only command changes are the small fixes in the last column.' Line 84 (brainstorm row): small fix 'None'. Line 159 (P1): 'the `--unattended` flag accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2'. Line 195 (AC-1.1): 'every command in sections 3.1-3.2 has a `## Unattended mode` section'.

sentence: An implementer who follows the stated text as written builds a ticket store that keeps a closed ticket for 3 years (R4) and deletes that same closed ticket one year after closing (R10). A ticket closed 18 months ago must be both present and absent, so the retention rule cannot be implemented as written.
evidence: Line 10 (R4): 'Support tickets are kept for 3 years after the ticket is closed.' Line 18 (R10): 'Closed support tickets are deleted one year after closing.'

sentence: Fails: the first branch needs the implementer to write an Orca verb into core files, and SA-2 permits only a mention in the contract file without saying whether a command-form string is allowed, so whether AC-C1 then fails is a guess. The second branch (stripping Orca verbs) is a choice the implementer makes, not what the text states. No stated text is determinately wrong.
evidence: Line 147 (SA-2): 'The only allowed mention of Orca in a changed command is as an example of a caller's question channel inside the contract file.' Line 172 (AC-C1) scans src/superclaude/core. Line 158 (P0) places the contract in src/superclaude/core/WORKER-CONTRACT.md.

sentence: Fails: the load row (line 112) and the decision at line 265 say load gets no report file and only a usage-line fix, while AC-1.1 (line 195) requires a section naming return-contract.yaml for every 3.2 command.
